assumptions: The Wilson hairpin collars share a reflection-plane footprint.
The normalized quotient is computed within the same finite family.
edges.direction: boundary OPE factors can introduce phase structure in normalized quotients
failure_modes: A nonzero quotient holonomy makes pairwise positivity insufficient.
A negative determinant falsifies the proposed positivity bridge.
edges.qualitative_behavior: boundary OPE factors can introduce phase structure in normalized quotients. Rate/regime character: finite-family and phase-sensitive. Convergence behavior: phase behavior must be computed before Schur quotient positivity can be trusted

assumptions: Q=Q*
Q_ii=1
quotient denominators are nonzero
Phi=arg(Q_12 Q_23 Q_31) modulo diagonal rephasing
all entries come from one finite reflected observable family
edges.direction: Every exact identity is valid only under the side-condition ledger; failing a side condition backtracks the branch before analytic promotion.
failure_modes: The determinant formula no longer licenses positivity conclusions.
Additional scale factors enter all minors and quotient comparisons.
The interface must backtrack to support-restricted or regularized quotient definitions.
A coordinate phase may be mistaken for a real obstruction.
The packet is quarantined as proxy algebra.
edges.qualitative_behavior: Side_condition_ledger: Hermitian normalization, nonzero quotient entries, phase convention, and finite-family scope decide whether the determinant and holonomy formulas apply.

assumptions: finite interface packet validates
falsifier preserves the same carrier side conditions except for the changed condition
edges.direction: Formula-derived falsifier shapes can demote pairwise-positivity, phase-removal, or modulus-only transfer branches.
failure_modes: pairwise minors pass while the 3x3 determinant is negative
no diagonal D removes all quotient phases on the support graph
real pairwise bounds do not produce PSD modulus quotient
the quotient identity fails to represent the continuum carrier without extra contact terms
edges.qualitative_behavior: Falsifier_shape: negative determinant with pairwise minors passing, nonzero cycle holonomy, negative modulus quotient minor, or nonzero additive contact prevents naive positivity transfer.

assumptions: The finite Wilson family is realized in the same reflected observable algebra.

failure_modes: The determinant failure is a toy artifact with no same-theory transfer certificate.
The determinant test is not realized by Yang-Mills observables.
The imagined situation is too remote from the target observable algebra.
The phase obstruction is an artifact of a proxy model.

edges.qualitative_behavior: nonzero holonomy or negative normalized determinant blocks naive positivity transfer. Rate/regime character: threshold-like. Convergence behavior: the branch must backtrack or quarantine if the finite-family determinant is negative

assumptions: Finite symbolic identities are valid.
Proof status remains blocked until same-theory analytic transfer is certified.
edges.direction: Exact finite algebra induces proof-relevant analytic estimates before any bounded numeric search is allowed.
failure_modes: B_ij is regulator-family dependent or cannot be realized in the same observable algebra.
Contacts shift the finite determinant sign or invalidate pairwise-to-family transfer.
A non-removable holonomy makes det(Q) negative in an admissible finite family.
Pairwise bounds hold while the three-by-three determinant is negative.
edges.qualitative_behavior: Analytic_obligation: the determinant and holonomy formulas become boundary OPE, additive contact, quotient phase, modulus PSD, and same-theory realization targets.

assumptions: Q is Hermitian.
Q_ii = 1 for i in {1,2,3}.
Q_ij = rho_ij exp(i theta_ij) with 0 <= rho_ij <= 1.
Phi = arg(Q_12 Q_23 Q_31) is invariant under diagonal rephasing.
edges.direction: The quotient holonomy Phi enters det(Q) through cos(Phi), so phase control can decide finite-family positivity.
failure_modes: pairwise minors hold but det(Q) < 0
Phi is not 0 modulo pi after diagonal rephasing
edges.linearity: trigonometric in Phi and multilinear in rho12 rho23 rho13
edges.qualitative_behavior: Symbolic_formula: det(Q)=1-rho12^2-rho23^2-rho13^2+2 rho12 rho23 rho13 cos(Phi). This controls a finite matrix interface, not Yang-Mills proof status.

assumptions: Regulated reflection positivity holds for every fixed cutoff.
The topology controls finite reflected observable families.
edges.direction: smaller cutoff should preserve positivity only if the positivity cone is closed
failure_modes: Reflection positivity leaks under cutoff removal.
The limiting topology is too weak for positivity closure.
edges.qualitative_behavior: smaller cutoff should preserve positivity only if the positivity cone is closed. Rate/regime character: not monotone without uniform topology. Convergence behavior: may converge to a positive Gram matrix only in the closed reflected-probe topology

assumptions: The correlator has a positive spectral representation.
The observable belongs to the reconstructed gauge-invariant algebra.
edges.direction: larger Euclidean time suppresses spectral components above the lower support
failure_modes: Decay is only fixed-regulator.
The observable sector is not dense or misses low-energy states.
edges.linearity: exponential when a positive spectral threshold is present
edges.qualitative_behavior: larger Euclidean time suppresses spectral components above the lower support. Rate/regime character: exponential when a positive spectral threshold is present. Convergence behavior: decay rate witnesses spectral support only after OS reconstruction and observable density

assumptions: A positive Hamiltonian and spectral measure are already constructed.
Vacuum contribution is removed.
edges.direction: larger mass scale gives faster long-time decay
failure_modes: The spectral measure has arbitrarily small non-vacuum support.
The correlator does not see the full excitation sector.
edges.linearity: exponential in t with rate bounded by m
edges.qualitative_behavior: larger mass scale gives faster long-time decay. Rate/regime character: exponential in t with rate bounded by m. Convergence behavior: C(t) is bounded by exp(-m t) times the observable norm when the spectral measure avoids (0,m)
